data.long_meaning: In Arabic, Maazuz means ‘protector’ or ‘the one who shelters’. This name is derived from the Arabic root ‘azaza’, which means ‘to protect’ or ‘to guard’. It is a name that invokes a sense of safety, security, and strength. The name Maazuz carries the meaning “Protector” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Maazuz usually hope their child will grow to embody protector and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Maazuz total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

data.cultural_impact: The name Maazuz holds significant cultural importance within Islamic communities as it is associated with the belief in Abdul-Muttalib, the ancestor of Prophet Muhammad (pbuh). According to Islamic tradition, Abdul-Muttalib was the protector and guardian of the Kaaba, which is the most sacred site in Islam. He is known for ensuring that food was always available for travelers and providing shelter to those in need. Thus, the name Maazuz in Arabic Islam represents a protector, someone who guards, and offers care and protection to those in need.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Maazuz reflects the significance of Allah the Protector, the Al-Malik Al-Khuddus (The Gracious and Generous King). It reminds us of Allah's promise to protect His believing servants: "And Allah has sent down tranquility into the hearts of the believers so that they do not add to their every misdeed; and as for the evildoers, their deceitfulness has added to their every misdeed" (Quran 48:4). The name Maazuz also serves as a reminder that we seek refuge in Allah, the Holy Protector, and trust in His promise to provide for us, protect us, and guide us.

modern_usage.modern_context: The Islamic name 'Maazuz' has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts, particularly in the realm of Islamic folklore and mythology. Maazuz is a jinn believed to reside in graves and guard them from intruders. In modern times, this figure has been the subject of various storytelling mediums, reflecting the growing interest in Islamic folklore and mythology. One popular platform for such content is YouTube, where creators share stories and interpretations of Maazuz and other Islamic figures through videos, animations, and voiceovers. Instagram is another platform where artists and illustrators share visually captivating depictions of Maazuz and other jinn. Lastly, podcasts offer a more immersive and in-depth exploration of the character and its significance in Islamic culture and belief systems.
